title: Review: Forces and their interactions; Work done and energy transfer; Forces and elasticity
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank for AQA GCSE Physics (8463) (review status in the bank: authored-gated-unreviewed). assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Joule (J)
items.clue: The unit of energy: one newton acting through one metre.

items.label: Work done
items.clue: Energy transferred when a force moves an object through a distance.

items.label: Centre of mass
items.clue: The single point at which the weight of an object may be considered to act.

items.label: Resultant force
items.clue: The single push or pull with the same effect as all those acting on an object together.

questions.stem: Which row gives the correct units for the quantities in W = m g?

options.text: W in newtons, m in kilograms and g in newtons per kilogram
W in kilograms, m in kilograms and g in newtons per kilogram
W in grams, m in kilograms and g in newtons per kilogram
W in newtons, m in kilograms and g in newtons of force

questions.explanation: These are the units exactly as the specification gives them: N, kg and N/kg.

questions.stem: Which row gives the correct units for the quantities in W = F s?

options.text: work in newtons, force in newtons, distance in metres
work in joules, force in newtons, distance in metres
work in watts, force in newtons, distance in metres
work in joules, force in newtons, time in seconds

questions.explanation: Work done, W, in joules, J; force, F, in newtons, N; distance, s, in metres.

questions.stem: A spring is stretched by a force and is not inelastically deformed. How does the elastic potential energy stored compare with the work done on the spring?

options.text: The energy stored is slightly less, because some energy is wasted.
The energy stored is much smaller, because a lot of energy is wasted.
No work is done at all, because the spring stays in one place.
The energy stored is equal to the work done on the spring by the force.

questions.explanation: The specification states that the work done and the elastic potential energy stored are equal in this case.

questions.stem: What does g stand for in the equation W = m g, and what is its unit?

options.text: Gravitational field strength, measured in newtons per kilogram
The force of gravity acting on the object, given in newtons
The weight of the object, measured in kilograms.
The strength of gravity there, measured in kilograms

questions.explanation: The specification gives gravitational field strength, g, in newtons per kilogram, N/kg.

questions.stem: A motor does 6000 N m of work. What is this work done in joules?

options.text: 6 J

questions.explanation: 1 joule = 1 newton-metre, so the number is unchanged: 6000 N m = 6000 J.

questions.stem: A spring is stretched so far that it is inelastically deformed. Which statement about the work done on the spring is correct?

options.text: The work done is greater than the elastic potential energy stored in it.
The work done is still exactly equal to the elastic potential energy stored.
The work done equals the energy stored, because they are always the same.
No work is done, because the spring does not spring back again.

questions.explanation: The equality holds only when the spring is not inelastically deformed; here some work is transferred elsewhere.

questions.stem: Why is the weight of an object drawn as a single arrow from one point on it?

options.text: Because weight acts where the object presses on the surface below.
Because the weight may be taken to act at the centre of mass.
Because gravity only acts on the part touching the ground.
Because a vector must always be drawn from the ground.

questions.explanation: The weight of an object may be considered to act at a single point, its centre of mass.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly defines one joule of work?

options.text: The work done when a force of 1 N acts for a time of 1 s
The force of 1 N needed to move an object through 1 m
The work done when 1 N of energy is given to a body
The work done when a force of 1 N causes a displacement of 1 m

questions.explanation: This is the specification definition: one joule of work is done when a force of one newton causes a displacement of one metre.

questions.stem: A force-extension graph for a spring is a straight line through the origin up to 8 N, and curves above 8 N. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The curved readings are anomalies and should be left out of the graph.
The relationship is linear up to 8 N and non-linear above 8 N.
The curved part shows the spring becoming stiffer as the load increases.
The curved part is caused by measurement errors in the larger readings.

questions.explanation: A straight line through the origin is a linear relationship; the curved region above 8 N is non-linear.

questions.stem: The weight of an object and the mass of an object are directly proportional. What does this mean?

options.text: Weight increases by a fixed amount each time mass increases.
Doubling the mass doubles the weight in the same field.
Weight just gets bigger by some amount when mass increases.
Weight and mass are equal when the units are ignored.

questions.explanation: Directly proportional means one quantity is a fixed multiple of the other, so the factor carries across.

questions.stem: A crane lifts a steel beam steadily upwards. Which statement best describes what happens as the crane's force does work on the beam?

options.text: Energy is transferred to the beam by the crane's force
New energy is created by the crane and passed to the beam
Energy is used up by the crane, so none reaches it
Force is stored inside the beam as it is lifted

questions.explanation: Doing work is a way of transferring energy; the joules of work done equal the joules transferred to the beam.

questions.stem: A spring with a spring constant of 2000 N/m is stretched by 8.0 cm, below its limit of proportionality. Using elastic potential energy = 0.5 × spring constant × (extension)^2, how much energy is stored?
